title: 13th Sitting of Third session of 2026
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem chaired part of the education bill debate)
summary: The sitting opened with a resolution from North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim seeking Parliament's view on the removal of three Supreme Court justices, which he said rested on unfounded allegations after the Prosecutor General declined to prosecute. Under the rules a vote is taken on accepting a resolution before debate; it failed 7 to 28, so the resolution was declared void. Parliament then continued debating the government's bill amending the Education Act (2020/24), introduced by Hura MP Dr. Anara Naeem, which would set the academic year start in law and introduce regulated homeschooling for children with special needs; members argued over homeschooling safeguards, spending and party politics. After a break the bill was accepted 41-0 and sent to a joint committee of the National Development and Heritage Committee and the Social Affairs Committee.

items.title: Attendance announcement
items.outcome: 25 present, 7 on leave, 7 on official travel

items.title: Approval of minutes of sittings 2026/3/7 to 2026/3/9

items.title: Change in Judiciary Committee membership

items.title: Committee deadline: bill amending the Tax Administration Act (Law 3/2010), Economic Committee
Resolution on the removal of three Supreme Court justices on allegedly unfounded charges (Mohamed Ibrahim)
Government bill amending the Education Act (Law 2020/24), presented by Dr. Anara Naeem
Vote on accepting the Education Act amendment bill
items.outcome: passed 41-0; sent to joint National Development and Heritage / Social Affairs committee

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill, saying it lets children with special needs learn at home online or with visiting teachers.
Criticised MDP members for calling it a 'jaariya bill' and urged consultation with the education minister in committee.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Presented resolution saying three Supreme Court justices were removed on unfounded allegations, citing the Prosecutor General's decision not to prosecute.
Argued judges' tenure is constitutionally protected and the Judicial Service Commission should be held accountable.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the education bill, citing high literacy rates and the need for laws that ease students' paths at every level.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Welcomed fixing the academic year in law and homeschooling for children with disabilities.
Rejected claims homeschooling would keep girls from education; suggested clarifying the wording of Article 16 in committee.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said the bill aims to cut education spending and that schools already rely on fundraising and sponsors.
Raised concerns about provisions affecting teachers' rights and reversing the academic calendar change.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Said homeschooling should be open to all parents able to afford it, not only children with disabilities.
Cited homeschooling practice in the US, UK, Ireland and India.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Opposed the bill, saying its conditions are left for the government to set without defined criteria.
Objected that the resolution was rejected without debate and condemned the Baarashu member's remarks about MDP.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Raised a point objecting to false statements made about a person not present in the chamber.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, saying the earlier move of the school year to mid-year burdened parents and students.
Welcomed the bill requiring the school year to start by January or February.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill, saying the current government expanded overseas study opportunities to all qualifying students.
Said the previous MDP government closed Hulhudhoo's long-standing school and called for online exam access.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the amendments, arguing the curriculum should shift to a research-based system and homeschooling helps children with disabilities.
Urged members to also support the Rasmaale project.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Closing remarks: thanked members and asked the committee to consider stakeholder and public input.
Said the bill aims to leave no child out of education, especially those needing special support.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2026/3/7 to 2026/3/9 declared accepted.
Kendhoo MP Mauroof Zakir appointed to the Judiciary Committee in place of North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim (MDP).
Resolution on removal of three Supreme Court justices not accepted (7-28) and declared void.
Education Act (2020/24) amendment bill accepted 41-0 and sent to a joint committee of the National Development and Heritage Committee and the Social Affairs Committee.
Next sitting announced for Wednesday 4 November 2026 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accepting the resolution on removal of three Supreme Court justices
Accepting the bill amending the Education Act (2020/24)
